title: Ostomy Supply Program Patient Account Terms: Payment Plans, Past-Due Holds, Write-Offs and Credits
content:
The Ostomy Supply Program sets the following patient account terms per payer tier. They govern payment plans, the past-due shipment hold, small-balance write-offs, financial-hardship waivers and credit-balance refunds.

## Definitions

- **Payment plan minimum balance** - the smallest patient balance, in USD, for which an interest-free payment plan may be requested.
- **Payment plan longest term** - the longest interest-free payment plan, in monthly installments; 0 means payment plans are not offered on the tier.
- **Payment plan minimum installment** - the smallest monthly installment accepted on a payment plan, in USD.
- **Past-due age** - the age, in calendar days after its posting date, at which an unpaid patient-balance posting becomes past due for the shipment hold test; 0 means shipments are never held for a past-due balance on the tier.
- **Past-due hold minimum** - the past-due amount, in USD, at or above which further shipments are held under the past-due rule.
- **Small-balance write-off ceiling** - the largest remaining patient balance, in USD, that is written off as a small balance instead of being statemented; 0.00 means no small-balance write-off on the tier.
- **Hardship waiver allowed** - whether a documented financial-hardship waiver of patient cost share may be granted case by case on the tier.
- **Hardship income ceiling** - the household income ceiling for a financial-hardship waiver, as a percent of the current HHS federal poverty guideline for the household size; a whole percent.
- **Credit-balance refund limit** - the time limit for refunding a customer credit balance (overpayment), in calendar days counted from the posting date of the entry that created the credit.

## Terms by tier

| Tier | Plan min. balance | Plan longest term | Plan min. installment | Past-due age | Past-due hold min. | Small-balance ceiling | Hardship waiver | Hardship income ceiling | Credit refund limit |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Ostomy Self-Pay Program | USD 150.00 | 0 (not offered) | USD 25.00 | 15 days | USD 50.00 | USD 0.00 | No | 200% | 30 days |
| Ostomy Commercial HMO Program | USD 150.00 | 6 months | USD 25.00 | 90 days | USD 75.00 | USD 4.99 | Yes | 200% | 30 days |
| Ostomy Commercial PPO Program | USD 150.00 | 6 months | USD 25.00 | 90 days | USD 75.00 | USD 4.99 | Yes | 200% | 30 days |
| Ostomy Medicare Advantage Program | USD 100.00 | 10 months | USD 20.00 | 120 days | USD 75.00 | USD 4.99 | Yes | 200% | 60 days |
| Ostomy Original Medicare Program | USD 100.00 | 10 months | USD 20.00 | 120 days | USD 75.00 | USD 0.00 | Yes | 200% | 60 days |
| Ostomy Medicaid Program | USD 100.00 | 0 (not offered) | USD 20.00 | 0 (never held) | USD 75.00 | USD 0.00 | No | 200% | 60 days |

## Reading the table

- Payment plans are not offered on the Ostomy Self-Pay Program or the Ostomy Medicaid Program, whose longest term is 0.
- Shipments on the Ostomy Medicaid Program are never held for a past-due balance, because its past-due age is 0; its past-due hold minimum has no effect.
- The small-balance write-off exists only on the Ostomy Commercial HMO Program, the Ostomy Commercial PPO Program and the Ostomy Medicare Advantage Program, each with a ceiling of USD 4.99.
- A hardship waiver may be considered on every tier except the Ostomy Self-Pay Program and the Ostomy Medicaid Program.
- *Hypothetical illustration:* a balance of USD 120.00 on the Ostomy Commercial PPO Program is below that tier's payment plan minimum balance of USD 150.00, while the same balance on the Ostomy Medicare Advantage Program meets that tier's minimum of USD 100.00.
